source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Reversal and total distance for linear velocity

hints: The particle stops when $v(t) = 0 \implies 6 - 2t = 0 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$.
Displacement at $t = 3$ is $\int_0^3 (6 - 2t)dt = 9\text{ m}$, and at $t = 5$ is $5\text{ m}$, so total distance is $9 + |5 - 9| = 13\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the turning point where velocity is zero:
$$v(t) = 6 - 2t = 0 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$

Integrate velocity to find the displacement function $s(t)$ with $s(0) = 0$:
$$s(t) = \int (6 - 2t)\,dt = 6t - t^2$$
$$s(3) = 6(3) - 3^2 = 18 - 9 = 9\text{ m}$$
$$s(5) = 6(5) - 5^2 = 30 - 25 = 5\text{ m}$$

Sum the absolute distances travelled before and after the turning point:
$$d = |s(3) - s(0)| + |s(5) - s(3)| = |9 - 0| + |5 - 9| = 9 + 4 = 13\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Locate the reversal time:
- Velocity changes sign at:
$$t = \frac{6}{2} = 3\text{ s}$$

Evaluate distance segments:
- Forward motion to $t = 3$: $9\text{ m}$
- Backward motion from $t = 3$ to $t = 5$: $4\text{ m}$:
$$d = 9 + 4 = 13\text{ m}$$
The particle covers a total distance of $13\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies instantaneous rest at $t = 3$ and integrates $v(t)$ to find displacements: $s(3) = 9$ and $s(5) = 5$.

Set displacement equal to zero to find when the particle returns to the origin:
$$4t^2 - t^3 = 0 \implies t^2(4 - t) = 0$$

$$t^2(4 - t) = 0 \implies t = 4\text{ s}$$

$$s(t) = 4t^2 - t^3$$
$$s\left(\frac{8}{3}\right) = 4\left(\frac{64}{9}\right) - \frac{512}{27} = \frac{256}{9} - \frac{512}{27} = \frac{768 - 512}{27} = \frac{256}{27}\text{ m}$$

$$d = 2 \times \frac{256}{27} = \frac{512}{27} \approx 19.0\text{ m}$$
The total distance is $\frac{512}{27}\text{ m}$.

hints: The particle stops when $3t^2 - 12 = 0 \implies t^2 = 4 \implies t = 2\text{ s}$.
Displacement function is $s(t) = t^3 - 12t$, so $s(2) = -16$ and $s(3) = -9$. Total distance is $|-16| + |-9 - (-16)| = 16 + 7 = 23\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the turning point where velocity is zero:
$$v(t) = 3t^2 - 12 = 0 \implies t^2 = 4 \implies t = 2\text{ s}$$

Integrate velocity to find $s(t)$ with $s(0) = 0$ and evaluate at $t = 2$ and $t = 3$:
$$s(t) = \int (3t^2 - 12)\,dt = t^3 - 12t$$
$$s(2) = 2^3 - 12(2) = 8 - 24 = -16\text{ m}$$
$$s(3) = 3^3 - 12(3) = 27 - 36 = -9\text{ m}$$

Calculate the total distance by summing the magnitudes of the displacements:
$$d = |s(2) - s(0)| + |s(3) - s(2)| = |-16 - 0| + |-9 - (-16)| = 16 + 7 = 23\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify direction change:
- Reverses direction at:
$$t = \sqrt{4} = 2\text{ s}$$

Sum distance magnitudes:
- Backward travel from $0$ to $-16$: $16\text{ m}$
- Forward return from $-16$ to $-9$: $7\text{ m}$:
$$d = 16 + 7 = 23\text{ m}$$
The total distance is $23\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Finds $v = 0$ at $t = 2$ and evaluates displacements: $s(2) = -16$ and $s(3) = -9$.

$$v(t) = 6t - 3t^2, \quad s(t) = 3t^2 - t^3$$

$$v(3) = 18 - 27 = -9\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The particle returns at $3\text{ s}$ with velocity $-9\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Reversal occurs when $v(t) = 0 \implies 2t(t - 3) = 0 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$.
Displacement is $s(t) = \int (2t^2 - 6t)dt = \frac{2}{3}t^3 - 3t^2$.
Substitute $t = 3$ to get $s(3) = 18 - 27 = -9\text{ m}$ and $t = 6$ to get $s(6) = 144 - 108 = 36\text{ m}$.
Total distance in $0 \le t \le 6$ is $|-9| + |36 - (-9)| = 9 + 45 = 54\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the turning point in the first phase by setting velocity to zero:
$$v(t) = 2t(t - 3) = 0 \implies t = 3\text{ s} \quad (t > 0)$$

Integrate velocity to find displacement $s(t)$ for $0 \le t \le 6$ with $s(0) = 0$:
$$s(t) = \int (2t^2 - 6t)\,dt = \frac{2}{3}t^3 - 3t^2$$
$$s(3) = \frac{2}{3}(27) - 3(9) = 18 - 27 = -9\text{ m} \quad (\text{minimum displacement})$$
$$s(6) = \frac{2}{3}(216) - 3(36) = 144 - 108 = 36\text{ m}$$

Calculate the total distance travelled by summing the magnitudes of the two parts:
$$d_1 = |s(3) - s(0)| + |s(6) - s(3)| = |-9 - 0| + |36 - (-9)| = 9 + 45 = 54\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine Phase 1 turning point:
- Motion reverses direction at:
$$t = 3\text{ s}$$

Evaluate Phase 1 positions:
- Minimum position:
$$s(3) = 18 - 27 = -9\text{ m}$$
- End position:
$$s(6) = 144 - 108 = 36\text{ m}$$

Compute distance in first 6 seconds:
- Backward then forward motion:
$$d_1 = 9 + 45 = 54\text{ m}$$
The particle covers $54\text{ m}$ in Phase 1.

ai_rubric.observable: Evaluates minimum displacement $s(3) = 18 - 27 = -9\text{ m}$ and displacement $s(6) = 144 - 108 = 36\text{ m}$.
Calculates total distance in first phase: $|-9 - 0| + |36 - (-9)| = 9 + 45 = 54\text{ m}$.

hints: In $6 \le t \le 10$, $v(t) = 54 - 3t > 0$ throughout (reversal would occur at $t = 18$), so the particle moves in one direction.
Displacement change in Phase 2 is $\int_6^{10} (54 - 3t)dt = [54t - 1.5t^2]_6^{10} = 120\text{ m}$ (or via trapezium rule $\frac{36 + 24}{2} \times 4 = 120\text{ m}$).
Displacement at $t = 10$ is $s(10) = 36 + 120 = 156\text{ m}$.
Total distance is Phase 1 distance plus Phase 2 distance: $54 + 120 = 174\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Check if velocity changes sign in the interval $6 \le t \le 10$:
$$v(6) = 54 - 3(6) = 36\text{ m s}^{-1} > 0$$
$$v(10) = 54 - 3(10) = 24\text{ m s}^{-1} > 0$$
$$\text{Since } v(t) = 0 \implies t = 18\text{ s}, \quad v(t) > 0 \text{ for all } t \in [6, 10], \quad \text{so no reversal occurs.}$$

Calculate the displacement change $\Delta s_2$ in the second phase:
$$\Delta s_2 = \int_6^{10} (54 - 3t)\,dt = \left[54t - 1.5t^2\right]_6^{10}$$
$$\Delta s_2 = \left[54(10) - 1.5(100)\right] - \left[54(6) - 1.5(36)\right] = (540 - 150) - (324 - 54) = 390 - 270 = 120\text{ m}$$

Find the displacement at $t = 10\text{ s}$ and the total distance:
$$s(10) = s(6) + \Delta s_2 = 36 + 120 = 156\text{ m}$$
$$d_{\text{total}} = d_1 + \Delta s_2 = 54 + 120 = 174\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Verify no turning point in Phase 2:
- Linear velocity remains positive throughout $6 \le t \le 10$:
$$v(6) = 36\text{ m s}^{-1}, \quad v(10) = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Compute distance in Phase 2:
- Using integration or trapezium area:
$$\Delta s_2 = \frac{36 + 24}{2} \times 4 = 120\text{ m}$$

Find final displacement and total distance:
- Position at $t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$s(10) = 36 + 120 = 156\text{ m}$$
- Overall distance travelled:
$$d_{\text{total}} = 54 + 120 = 174\text{ m}$$
A total distance of $174\text{ m}$ is covered.

ai_rubric.observable: States that $v(t) = 54 - 3t > 0$ for all $t \in [6, 10]$ (since $v = 0$ at $t = 18$), so no reversal occurs.
Obtains total distance across the entire $10\text{ s}$: $54 + 120 = 174\text{ m}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Complete journey with multiple reversals and return to origin

hints: Instantaneous rest occurs when $v(t) = 0 \implies 0.12(t - 2)(t - 8) = 0$.
Solve for rest times: $t = 2\text{ s}$ and $t = 8\text{ s}$.
Displacement is $s(t) = 0.12\left(\frac{1}{3}t^3 - 5t^2 + 16t\right) = 0.04t^3 - 0.6t^2 + 1.92t$.
Substitute $t = 2$ to find $s(2) = 1.76\text{ m}$, and $t = 8$ to find $s(8) = -2.56\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the times of instantaneous rest by setting velocity to zero:
$$v(t) = 0.12(t - 2)(t - 8) = 0 \implies t = 2\text{ s} \quad \text{and} \quad t = 8\text{ s}$$

Integrate velocity to determine the displacement function $s(t)$ with $s(0) = 0$:
$$s(t) = \int 0.12(t^2 - 10t + 16)\,dt = 0.12\left(\frac{1}{3}t^3 - 5t^2 + 16t\right) = 0.04t^3 - 0.6t^2 + 1.92t$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Locate rest instants:
- Factored velocity roots:
$$t = 2\text{ s}, \quad t = 8\text{ s}$$

Evaluate displacement at rest points:
- Integrating velocity:
$$s(2) = 1.76\text{ m}, \quad s(8) = -2.56\text{ m}$$
The particle is at $1.76\text{ m}$ and $-2.56\text{ m}$ respectively.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies instantaneous rest times from factorised velocity: $t = 2\text{ s}$ and $t = 8\text{ s}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Complete journey with multiple reversals and return to origin

hints: Since $s(2) = +1.76 > 0$ and $s(8) = -2.56 < 0$, the particle crosses $s = 0$ between $t = 2$ and $t = 8$.
Displacement at $t = 10$ is $s(10) = 40 - 60 + 19.2 = -0.8\text{ m}$.
Segment 1 ($0 \le t \le 2$): distance $= 1.76\text{ m}$.
Segment 2 ($2 \le t \le 8$): distance $= | -2.56 - 1.76 | = 4.32\text{ m}$.
Segment 3 ($8 \le t \le 10$): distance $= | -0.8 - (-2.56) | = 1.76\text{ m}$. Total distance is $1.76 + 4.32 + 1.76 = 7.84\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Demonstrate return to origin:
$$\text{At } t = 2, \quad s(2) = +1.76\text{ m} > 0$$
$$\text{At } t = 8, \quad s(8) = -2.56\text{ m} < 0$$
$$\text{Because } s(t) \text{ is continuous, there must exist a time } t^* \in (2, 8) \text{ where } s(t^*) = 0, \text{ so } P \text{ passes through } O.$$

Calculate the distance travelled in each of the three monotone intervals:
$$\text{Interval } [0, 2]: \quad d_1 = |s(2) - s(0)| = |1.76 - 0| = 1.76\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Interval } [2, 8]: \quad d_2 = |s(8) - s(2)| = |-2.56 - 1.76| = 4.32\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Interval } [8, 10]: \quad d_3 = |s(10) - s(8)| = |-0.80 - (-2.56)| = 1.76\text{ m}$$

Sum the interval distances to obtain the total distance travelled:
$$d = d_1 + d_2 + d_3 = 1.76 + 4.32 + 1.76 = 7.84\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Show return to origin:
- Displacement changes sign between $t = 2$ and $t = 8$:
$$s(2) = +1.76\text{ m} \implies s(8) = -2.56\text{ m} \implies s(t^*) = 0$$

Calculate final position:
- At $t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$s(10) = 40 - 60 + 19.2 = -0.8\text{ m}$$

Sum three distance segments:
- First forward segment: $1.76\text{ m}$
- Middle backward segment: $4.32\text{ m}$
- Final forward segment: $1.76\text{ m}$:
$$d = 1.76 + 4.32 + 1.76 = 7.84\text{ m}$$
The total distance travelled is $7.84\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Notes that $s(2) = 1.76 > 0$ and $s(8) = -2.56 < 0$, so by continuity $s(t) = 0$ occurs in $2 < t < 8$ (return to origin).
Partitions total distance across the three monotone segments: $d = |s(2) - s(0)| + |s(8) - s(2)| + |s(10) - s(8)|$.
